task: Display the switch’s complete MAC address table so you can compare VLAN, entry type and learned port.

teaching.hint: Choose the forwarding table rather than the IPv4-to-MAC cache.
teaching.takeaway: Dynamic rows record source addresses learned on a port within a VLAN. They do not list IP routes, and a host need not be directly attached to the displayed port.

task: Find the MAC-table entry for 0050.56be.1a2b without displaying unrelated addresses.

teaching.hint: Filter by the full destination MAC you are tracing.
teaching.takeaway: Read the VLAN, entry type and port together. An uplink points toward the host; it does not establish that the host is directly cabled to this switch.

task: Several hosts sit behind the switch connected to SW1 Fa0/24. Display only MAC-table entries associated with that local uplink.

teaching.hint: Filter by the local interface, not by a neighbor’s address.
teaching.takeaway: Several different source MACs on an uplink are normal. This view answers which learned paths use that port; it does not prove each host is currently reachable.

task: This switch already has several VLANs. Display only the learned or configured MAC entries for VLAN 10.

teaching.hint: MAC learning is separated by VLAN.
teaching.takeaway: A MAC lookup belongs to a VLAN’s forwarding context. This command inspects existing entries; it neither creates VLAN 10 nor assigns access ports to it.
